source: d678139

# Overview

## What this is

A single Terraform configuration (kind: IaC, [reference/infra.md](../reference/infra.md)). There is
no application code, no CI/CD, and no README in the repository — the whole of the current state is
three `.tf` files:

- `main.tf` — the root module.
- `modules/app/main.tf` — a child module.
- `modules/network/main.tf` — a child module.

## Parts and how they talk

The root module (`main.tf`) declares one provider and calls both child modules unconditionally
([reference/infra.md](../reference/infra.md)):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  root["root (main.tf)"] --> app["app (./modules/app)"]
  root --> network["network (./modules/network)"]
  root -.->|provider aws ~> 5.0, region us-east-1| aws[(AWS)]
  app -->|aws_instance x2| aws
  network -->|aws_vpc x1| aws
```

- **root** (`main.tf:14-16, 18-20`): calls `module "network"` and `module "app"`, each with only a
  `source` argument — no `variables.tf`, no `input` arguments, and no module `output` blocks exist
  anywhere in the repository.
- **network** (`modules/network/main.tf:1-3`): one resource, `aws_vpc.main` (`cidr_block =
  "10.0.0.0/16"`). It declares no outputs.
- **app** (`modules/app/main.tf:1-9`): two resources, `aws_instance.web` and `aws_instance.worker`
  (same `ami = "ami-123456"`, `instance_type = "t3.micro"`). Neither instance sets
  `subnet_id`, `vpc_security_group_ids`, or any other attribute that would place it inside the VPC
  the `network` module creates.

**Finding, not invented — directly readable in the three files above:** `network` and `app` are
called side by side by `root` but are not wired to each other. `network`'s VPC has no consumer, and
`app`'s instances carry no reference to it, so this configuration does not connect the two modules'
resources. Applying it as-is would create `aws_instance.web`/`worker` in the account's default VPC
(AWS's standard behavior for an `aws_instance` with no subnet specified), alongside an unused
`aws_vpc` from the `network` module. See [risks.md](risks.md).

## Provider

One provider is configured, in the root module only: `hashicorp/aws`, version constraint `~> 5.0`,
region `us-east-1` (`main.tf:1-12`, [reference/infra.md](../reference/infra.md)). Child modules
declare no `terraform { required_providers }` block of their own and use the provider configuration
implicitly inherited from the root — this is why
[reference/deps.md](../reference/deps.md) flags `aws` as having no "production import site" and
`unused: yes`: the generic dependency extractor looks for explicit references into a module and does
not model Terraform's implicit-provider-inheritance mechanism. The provider is in fact used, by both
child modules' resources. GAP: whether any other provider (e.g. for remote state locking) is
configured outside the three tracked `.tf` files could not be determined — none exists in the
checked-in code.

## State and credentials

No `backend` block appears in `main.tf`, so Terraform defaults to the `local` backend: state is read
from and written to a `terraform.tfstate` file in the working directory, not a remote/shared store.
No AWS credentials are configured in code (`provider "aws"` only sets `region`); Terraform resolves
credentials through its standard provider chain (environment variables, shared config/credentials
file, instance role, etc.). GAP: which of those sources is actually used, and who holds the
credentials, is operational information not present in the repository. See
[secrets.md](secrets.md).

## Pipeline

[reference/delivery.md](../reference/delivery.md) reports "no `.github/workflows` found" — there is
no CI/CD automation in this repository. `plan`/`apply` are run by whatever process an operator uses
outside of this checkout; GAP: how (locally, a separate pipeline, a different tool) is not shown
here.

## What could not be rendered

The C4 context view could not be rendered in this environment: the renderer needs network access to
`registry.npmjs.org` and the sandbox denied it ([_run/run.md](_run/run.md)). The model is still
recorded as text in [model/hand.c4](model/hand.c4) and [model/generated.c4](model/generated.c4); a
network-enabled run of `arch run` would produce the image. See [_run/review.md](_run/review.md) for
the full explanation — this is a tooling limitation of this run, not a fact about the Terraform
configuration itself.

## Everything in this repository

For completeness, the full resource/provider/module inventory this overview draws on is generated at
[reference/infra.md](../reference/infra.md); nothing in this file goes beyond what is listed there or
directly readable in the three `.tf` files named above.
